Strong roaming synergy with TF (+4.6%) enables map pressure. Into the enemy comp, she locks down Ahri and provides isolation tools. A solid, reliable pick.

Overall synergy is near-zero (-0.006), with critical negatives vs Elise (-0.105) and Jinx (-0.065) that aren't offset by Nautilus pairing (+0.201). You'd be picking into the matchup (dominates Gnar at +25.8%) rather than into your team composition. The redundant engage problem is real: Nautilus + Elise + K'Sante = three initiation sources fighting for priority. Only recommend if you're explicitly locking in K'Sante for matchup value and accepting the composition risk. Consider this a 'high floor, lower ceiling' pick for your specific draft.

Ornn doesn't appear in the specialist recommendations but deserves consideration as a composition-complete pick. He solves three critical problems: (1) Provides tankiness + peel for Jinx without redundant engage like K'Sante, (2) AP damage scaling for your AD-heavy comp (Jax/Jinx/K'Sante alternatives), (3) Item upgrade utility amplifies your entire team's damage. Ornn synergizes well with Nautilus (mutual frontline), Twisted Fate (sustain + utility), and most critically, Elise (doesn't compete for early game resources). While not featured in pro meta as heavily as Jax/Camille, Ornn is a flex pick that completes your team's scaling profile. Into Gnar, Ornn scales similarly and can itemize for the matchup.

Sion is another composition anchor that deserves strong consideration over lower-synergy stat picks. He provides: (1) Massive HP scaling that synergizes with Nautilus engage (easier for him to lock targets), (2) AP scaling for your team's damage distribution (alongside Elise, Twisted Fate), (3) Zero redundancy with Elise's early game (Sion prefers scaling), (4) Excellent Nautilus + Sion teamfight patterns (mutual hard CC). While individual matchup stats vs Gnar/Sejuani are less impressive than K'Sante, Sion's team enablement and scaling profile better align with your composition's mid-to-late game win condition. A 'system pick' that makes everyone better rather than a stat optimizer.

Patch context: 59% WR, +3 base AD and 60s Package CD reduction directly address laning weakness vs Nautilus (stats agent validation). Synergy: 0.76 rating with elite Sejuani pairing (1.0 WR, +0.40 delta) and proven Thresh synergy (60% WR together). Fills critical team gap—your comp lacked reliable AP scaling. Package cooldown buff enables mid-game teamfight follow-up when Sejuani engages. Early-patch momentum + patch-targeted buffs override all other considerations.

Not mentioned by specialists, but fits critical gaps: Jhin provides utility (root, 4th shot execute) that works with Thresh hooks and enables Sejuani follow-up without the Thresh synergy problems of Varus. Utility ADC profile aligns with your peel-heavy comp better than raw DPS carries. Recommendation: If Corki unavailable and you want safer team synergy than Varus/Kog'Maw, Jhin is a fallback that doesn't create composition friction. Requires champion pool availability.

Recommendation: Fallback if Corki banned; safer pick than meta alternatives with poor team fit.

Consensus pick across all three agents (stats: 52% WR, 54 games; pro: 50% WR, 14-pick trend; patch: benefits from Syndra removal). Patch-driven pick with major buffs (Base AD +3, Package cooldown 240s, 59% WR). Exceptional synergy with Sejuani (100% WR, +0.40 delta) validates engagement into organized play. Smart meta pick despite weak 41% solo WR. Phenomenal synergy with Sejuani (+0.217, 75% WR across 12 games) and Nautilus (+0.204, 75% WR across 8 games). Composition multiplier—he enables your hard-CC team to convert advantages, justifying the individual stat underperformance.

Strong matchup delta strategy (+17.3% avg into enemy comp, especially Gnar). Excellent Nautilus pairing (+20.1% synergy). Rumble is the optimal pick for this team composition. Multiple agents support this: Pro meta (62.5% WR, trending), Stats (51% WR with +29% delta vs K'Sante, +34.8% vs Caitlyn), and critically, Synergy analysis (0.71 score with +0.21 overall delta). Aurora + Rumble achieve perfect synergy (1.0 WR, +0.45 delta), and Rumble + Sejuani synergize strongly (+0.19 delta). Unlike Nautilus/Zeri, Rumble doesn't clash with your core engine. His AoE zone control patches your lack of backline peel against Syndra/Caitlyn while amplifying Sejuani's engage reliability. The pre-existing Sejuani-Thresh weakness is not Rumble's fault; he's the best fit among all candidates to work within that constraint.

Jax is the safe, scalable alternative with strong pro meta validation (92 score: 64% WR, 28% pick rate in pro play). However, this is manageable in late-game scenarios where Thresh setup enables Jax to scale into a secondary damage threat. Pick Jax if you prioritize reliability and late-game insurance over compositional optimization.

Pick Renekton only if you commit to early-game snowball strategy and accept that mid-game teamfighting (your presumed strength with CC chains) will be suboptimal.

The recommendation works only if your team commits to splitting rather than coordinated teamfighting. In a comp built around Sejuani + Thresh engage, this split-focus creates strategic tension. Pick only if you expect to leverage her 1v1 pressure and objective control rather than rely on 5v5 synergy.

He's a 'doesn't hurt' addition rather than a composition optimizer. Pick Maokai only if enemy draft forces you to pivot toward tankier frontlines and you're willing to sacrifice synergistic multipliers for macro safety.
